The instructions for this hydrogel mask are incredibly clear, making the application process completely straightforward. On clean-shaven skin, like my girlfriend's face, the mask fits flawlessly with absolutely zero gaps. It hugs the contours of the face perfectly. Just keep in mind that this is a deep-treatment mask. It took about 3 to 4 hours to completely dry down, turn translucent, and absorb fully into the skin. The main challenge comes if you have a trimmed beard or facial hair. The hydrogel material cannot grip hair, so the lower half of the mask will not stick properly and tends to fall off. Only the upper section secured well to my forehead and upper cheeks.However, we found some great creative workarounds so nothing went to waste! My girlfriend applied the remaining jaw and chin section to my neck 😂, which worked beautifully. We also used the tiny punch-out eye and mouth patches creatively, placing the extra pieces above my eyebrows and using the mouth cutout across the bridge of my nose for targeted hydration. Pros:Truly delivers a noticeable boost in skin hydration and plumpness. Leaves the skin feeling incredibly smooth, refreshed, and deeply nourished. High-quality ingredients that genuinely work, offering great value for money. Cons: Not beard-friendly, as the lower half slides off facial hair. Requires 3–4 hours to dry, so it is best used when you have plenty of time or as an overnight mask. Final Verdict:If you have a smooth, clean-shaven face, this mask is an easy 5-star product because the fit and skin benefits are flawless. If you have a beard, the lower half simply won't stick. However, because it is highly effective and versatile enough to be repurposed on your neck and nose, it still deserves a solid 4 stars. Highly recommended, but beard wearers beware! This isn’t just a basic face wash — it effectively cleans while still keeping my skin feeling soft and hydrated, which is rare for a cleanser. Unlike many cleansers that leave my skin tight or dry, this one feels soothing and comfortable right after rinsing. Overall Thoughts: This is a simple but highly effective daily cleanser that manages to balance deep cleaning with hydration — ideal if you want something that won’t strip or irritate your skin. I’ve enjoyed how comfortable it feels on my face, and I’ll definitely purchase again. Highly recommend if you’re normal-to-dry skin or just want a gentle, everyday clean without tightness. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. Dopo aver provato praticamente tutti i detergenti CeraVe, posso dire che questa è la versione che preferisco in assoluto per la mia pelle. Ho una pelle mista, quindi con alcune zone che tendono a lucidarsi e diventare più oleose e altre che invece possono risultare più secche. Per questo ho sempre cercato un detergente che riuscisse a pulire bene senza lasciarmi quella sensazione di pelle "tirata" dopo il lavaggio. Nel corso del tempo ho provato praticamente tutte le versioni della linea CeraVe. Ho iniziato anche dall'olio detergente, proprio perché cercavo qualcosa di estremamente delicato. Mi è piaciuto, soprattutto per la sensazione che lasciava e per la profumazione, ma personalmente non era quello con cui mi trovavo meglio. Ho poi provato la crema detergente e, invece, non sono riuscito ad apprezzarla particolarmente. Soprattutto in estate, la sensazione durante l'utilizzo mi risultava troppo simile a quella di spalmare una crema sul viso e non era la tipologia di detersione che cercavo. Con la Schiuma Detergente, invece, ho trovato finalmente il compromesso che cercavo. LA SCHIUMA FA DAVVERO LA DIFFERENZA La prima cosa che si nota è ovviamente la consistenza: a contatto con l'acqua il detergente produce una bella schiuma. Ora, dal punto di vista scientifico, più schiuma non significa necessariamente più pulizia. È un aspetto importante perché spesso associamo inconsciamente una grande quantità di schiuma a un prodotto più efficace. Però c'è anche un aspetto più pratico e personale: a me la schiuma piace. Durante la skincare trovo molto più piacevole massaggiare una schiuma sul viso rispetto a una crema o a un olio. È una piccola cosa, ma secondo me il fatto che una routine sia piacevole da fare aumenta anche la probabilità di riuscire a mantenerla con costanza. La skincare, alla fine, non è soltanto una questione di ingredienti: anche la sensorialità del prodotto conta nell'esperienza quotidiana. PERCHÉ È ADATTA ALLA PELLE MISTA La formula è pensata per detergere rimuovendo sebo, impurità e residui senza compromettere eccessivamente la barriera cutanea. CeraVe utilizza in questa linea ceramidi e acido ialuronico, ingredienti interessanti soprattutto perché la detersione non dovrebbe limitarsi a "sgrassare" la pelle, ma dovrebbe cercare di mantenere un buon equilibrio tra pulizia e comfort. Le ceramidi, in particolare, sono lipidi naturalmente presenti nella barriera cutanea e svolgono un ruolo importante nel mantenimento della funzione barriera. È quindi sensato trovarle all'interno di una linea cosmetica che punta a detergere senza lasciare la pelle inutilmente impoverita. Il detergente contiene inoltre niacinamide, ingrediente molto versatile che viene utilizzato frequentemente nelle formulazioni destinate alle pelli miste o impure. Una cosa che apprezzo è proprio il fatto che, dopo il risciacquo, non mi rimane quella sensazione di "pelle che tira" che personalmente associo a una detersione troppo aggressiva. COME LO UTILIZZO Ne basta davvero poco. Inumidisco il viso, erogo una piccola quantità di prodotto e lo massaggio delicatamente sulla pelle, senza sfregare eccessivamente. Poi risciacquo con acqua. Non vedo la necessità di utilizzare una quantità enorme di detergente: la schiuma si distribuisce bene e una confezione da 473 ml dura davvero a lungo. Ed è proprio questo uno dei motivi per cui considero questo formato particolarmente conveniente. 473 ML: UN FORMATO CHE FA LA DIFFERENZA Questa secondo me è una delle caratteristiche più sottovalutate. Molti detergenti che mi incuriosiscono, soprattutto alcuni prodotti coreani, vengono venduti in confezioni da 150, 200 o 250 ml. Non è necessariamente un problema, ma quando si utilizza un detergente ogni giorno, mattina e/o sera, il prodotto finisce abbastanza rapidamente. Qui invece abbiamo 473 ml, quindi quasi mezzo litro. Considerando che ne basta poco ad ogni utilizzo, una confezione mi dura veramente parecchio. Per una skincare quotidiana è un vantaggio enorme, soprattutto se si vuole evitare di ricomprare continuamente il detergente. LA MIA ESPERIENZA Dopo aver provato praticamente tutta la gamma detergente CeraVe, questa è quella che ricomprerei più volentieri. Non perché sia necessariamente "la migliore" per qualsiasi tipo di pelle, ma perché è quella che si adatta meglio alle mie esigenze. La mia pelle mista ha bisogno di una detersione che mi faccia sentire il viso pulito senza trasformare il lavaggio in un momento in cui la pelle viene aggredita. La schiuma rende inoltre l'utilizzo molto piacevole e il formato da 473 ml permette di utilizzarlo quotidianamente senza preoccuparsi troppo dei consumi. PRO: ✅ Ottimo compromesso per pelle mista. ✅ Schiuma piacevole e facile da distribuire. ✅ Non lascia, nel mio caso, una sensazione eccessiva di pelle che tira. ✅ Formula con ceramidi, acido ialuronico e niacinamide. ✅ 473 ml: formato molto più conveniente rispetto a molti detergenti più piccoli. ✅ Ne basta poco e quindi dura davvero tanto. CONTRO: ❌ Se non amate i detergenti schiumogeni, probabilmente questa non è la consistenza che state cercando. ❌ La schiuma è piacevole ma non significa automaticamente che il prodotto deterge più di un detergente che fa poca schiuma. VALUTAZIONE FINALE Dopo aver provato praticamente tutti i detergenti CeraVe, questa è la versione che sceglierei nuovamente. Per la mia pelle mista trovo che sia il compromesso migliore tra sensazione di pulizia, comfort e piacevolezza durante l'utilizzo. Non mi lascia quella sensazione eccessivamente sgrassata che personalmente non amo, ma allo stesso tempo mi dà la sensazione di aver lavato bene il viso. Il vero punto forte, però, è l'insieme: buona sensorialità, formula pensata per rispettare la barriera cutanea, poca quantità necessaria e un formato enorme da 473 ml. Non sarà il detergente più "instagrammabile" o quello con la confezione più particolare, ma dopo averne provati così tanti, alla fine mi sono reso conto che quello che cerco nella skincare quotidiana è proprio questo: un prodotto che funziona, che mi piace

For the £23 I bought it for I'd say this is definitely not the worst investment I've ever made, and it absolutely does give me a far better tooth clean than any manual brush ever could. From that perspective it absolutely does what I bought it for. That being said though, I think I have to echo a lot of what other people have been saying about it, from the point of view of its downsides. I havent had quite the egregious battery life other people seem to have been experiencing, but I'd also hesitate to call the battery life "good". I live by myself, and I manage to get anywhere from two to three days out of it before it needs charging again. Its not absolutely terrible and I bought it knowing the battery life was a weak point, but if you have a full family thats using it then the battery won't last very long at all. This is a problem, considering that there's no way to know when the battery is getting low other than just how strong the motor feels when you're using it. Looking at the instructions, it seems like other models have an LED on them, but this one doesnt even have a single one. This both means that its hard to get an exact idea of when the battery needs charging, and also means you wont know when exactly its done charging either (I think maybe some people are experiencing poor battery life because they arent leaving it on for long enough, precisely because of that). You sort of just have to guess at when it might be done or check how strong the motor feels. Dont get me wrong, I like that its simple and I dont think its inherently a bad product - I intend to keep it an use it even with its flaws, just because it does everything I need it to, only really cost the equivalent of a few packets of toothburshes, and having the integrated timer is really useful. However I feel like they made it a little too simple for its own good. Not having even a single LED on there does kind of harm the functionality, given that the battery life isnt exactly stellar to begin with. I'm ok with that on balance since I'm the only one using it here, but it may well be worth it to most people to move slightly further up the like to a slightly higer end brush. I feel like its also worth noting, while we're on the subject, that the brush's charger only has a shaver plug connector, and it doesnt include an adapter for a standard wall socket. Thats fine if you have a shaver plug, but I feel like to an extent those are a dying breed so most people will also need a shaver plug adapter to use a normal socket with it, which is worth noting since it adds to the cost and it isnt really mentioned on the product page (albeit not especially significantly). I genuinely recommend it to everyone! This is, without exaggeration, my absolute favourite mascara of all time. I've tried more expensive mascaras in the past, and honestly, none of them have even come close to how good this one is. For the price, I genuinely think this is one of the best mascaras you can buy. I always get it in the black shade, and I have absolutely no complaints whatsoever. Every single time I wear this mascara, I get compliments on my eyelashes. I've genuinely had people ask me what mascara I'm wearing, and some people have even thought I was wearing fake lashes because of how long and full they look! The length it gives my lashes is honestly amazing, but it's not just length either. It gives them really good volume and makes them look so much more dramatic. One of my favourite things about it is the lift it gives as well. People have asked me if I've curled my eyelashes, but I literally never curl them. I don't even feel like I need to when I'm wearing this mascara because it makes them look so lifted and curled on its own. It also layers really well, which I love. You don't need to spend ages applying loads and loads of coats either. Just a couple of layers and the difference is honestly amazing. It's quick and easy to apply, but you can also build it up if you want a more dramatic look without it feeling like you have to fight with the mascara to get the effect you want. Another massive plus for me is how easily it comes off at the end of the day. I've used mascaras before that are so stubborn you practically need to declare war on your eyelashes to remove them, and you have to use loads of makeup remover and still end up with little bits left behind. This one is completely different. I usually just wash my face in the shower, and it comes off really easily with water, which I personally find so convenient. It also lasts me really well. I would say one tube lasts me around two months, possibly even a little longer depending on how often I'm wearing it, which makes it even better value for money. I've bought much more expensive mascaras before thinking they must surely be better, but I've honestly been disappointed so many times. This mascara proves that you really don't need to spend loads of money to get amazing results. I genuinely recommend this to everyone who asks me what mascara they should buy. If you're looking for something that gives you serious length, volume and lift without spending a ridiculous amount of money, this is the one. Five stars, no complaints, and I will continue buying it again and again. Love, love, love, love, love! " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. In the event of the CO alarm sounding, follow these 3 steps: VENTILATE : Keep calm; open doors and windows to ventilate your home. Stop using fuel-burning appliances and turn them off. EVACUATE : Evacuate the property immediately. RING FOR HELP: If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. Do not use appliances until they have been checked by an expert. Get medical help for anyone suffering the effects of CO poisoning. What are the symptoms of CO poisoning? Symptoms of CO poisoning include headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea and vomiting, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, seizures, chest pain, disorientation, and loss of consciousness. Who should I call in the event of a CO leak? If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. What are the sources of CO? The common sources of Carbon Monoxide (CO) are cookers, fires, boilers, oil and gas boilers, portable generators, oil or solid fuel cookers, gas or paraffin heaters, barbecues (BBQs), clogged chimneys, wood or gas fireplaces, cigarette smoke or any fossil fuel‑burning appliances. After the gas was disconnected his symptoms significantly improved (although they haven't disappeared entirely). Headaches, dizziness and nausea are symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning and I now suspect there had been a low-level carbon monoxide leak for months, which was making him sick, but not enough to activate the alarm. I have learnt that carbon monoxide alarms must activate if the levels exceed a certain quantity within a certain time period, but the alarms are not required to activate if carbon monoxide levels exceed healthy amounts but then reduce within the permitted time limit. This means someone could potentially have repeated intermittent exposure to toxic amounts of carbon monoxide without carbon monoxide alarms necessarily activating. Adjust heat, set timers, or switch modes without leaving your seat — comfort is now just one click away. Powerful heat that fits everywhere: Dreo space heaters for indoor combines Hyperamics 1500W advanced PTC system with a new heat funnel design to deliver heat within seconds and enhance warm air circulation for up to 200% farther reach than traditional heaters. Unbreakable safety: Dreo goes beyond the unexpected to deliver peace of mind with every room heater. The innovative tilt-detection sensor improves accuracy and reliability for better tip-over protection, and built with V0 flame retardant materials, overheat protection, and safety plug. Ultimate temperature control: The enhanced NTC chipset brings more precision to turn your space heater with thermostat into a smart heating powerhouse, allowing you to set heat on a wider range from 5-35℃ with ±1℃ increments, saving you energy while keeping you comfortable. Cozy quietness: No more choosing between quiet or warmth, Dreo's heater for bedroom warms quietly thanks to its brushless DC motor with frictionless performance and a winglet fan design that reduces turbulence, reducing noise to only 34dB. Fits into your lifestyle: This portable heater handle makes it easier to carry and is equipped with multiple heating levels and modes to heat as you like (Power heat, ECO, Fan Only). It also features handy extras for a hassle-free experience (12-hour timer, mute, child lock, and memory function). Upgraded Control Panel: This new version features a silk-screened button design that stands out with a white-on-black background for enhanced visibility and better user experience. Blocked nose, head cold, congestion, headache, fever, aches, and pain. How to relive symptoms of a cold? You can help relieve a blocked nose with Sudafed decongestant spray or tablets. You can ease aches and pains with painkillers like Paracetamol, or Ibuprofen. Sudafed capsule products contain paracetamol and a decongestant. How long does a cold last? It can vary, but you should begin to feel better in about a week or two. See your GP if your symptoms don't improve after 10 days. What is Sinusitis? A condition in which the cavities around the nasal passages become inflamed and swollen. Acute sinusitis can be triggered by a cold or allergies and may resolve on its own. What causes a blocked nose? A blocked nose occurs when the nose lining becomes inflamed and swollen. This causes the nasal passages to become narrower and therefore more easily blocked up. Now all I can smell is my laundry detergent, and that’s good enough! This cleaner is suitable for both front-loading and top-loading machines, and it’s great for prolonging the life of your appliance by preventing limescale and dirt build-up. If you’ve been dealing with an awful odour in your washing machine like I was, I can’t recommend this product enough. I wish I had found it sooner. It would have saved me so much frustration. Its targeted, self-acting spray has a bleaching action and works in around 30 minutes, helping remove stains without scrubbing on compatible surfaces. Test first in an inconspicuous place before applying Product description Product Description HG Mould Spray is a fast-acting black mould remover for walls and household surfaces affected by visible mould, mildew, fungus and algae in damp areas. Its targeted, self-acting spray has a bleaching action and works in around 30 minutes, helping remove stains without scrubbing on compatible surfaces. Use it indoors in bathrooms, showers, toilets, kitchens, cellars, basements and saunas on suitable plastered walls, tiles, grout, silicone joints, window frames and other compatible surfaces. It can also be used outdoors around compatible swimming pools, facades, balconies, plant boxes and garden ornaments, excluding wood. One 500ml bottle treats approximately 2–3 m² of wall surface or 6–8 m² of tile grout. Ensure good ventilation and wear suitable rubber or plastic gloves. Remove the safety clip or unlock the nozzle. Spray from approximately 3–5cm away and leave for 30 minutes. Clean the treated area with water and a sponge. For stubborn stains, reapply and leave for a further 30 minutes. For silicone joints, wash off after 30 minutes and repeat if necessary. Always test first in an inconspicuous area. Permanent brown discolouration may occur on elastic grouting, badly glazed tiles or old tiles with hairline cracks. Do not use on wood, coloured surfaces, ceilings, clothing, paintwork, plastic shower trays, vertical blinds, aluminium, stainless steel or other sensitive metals. Avoid splashes and do not reuse the bottle. Never mix with other cleaning products, as dangerous chlorine gas may be released. Wash hands after handling. Store and transport cool, dark and upright. Very toxic to aquatic life; avoid release into the environment. Keep out of reach of children and read the label before use. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. 3/5 stars A Promising Blend with a Misleading Punch I was genuinely excited to try this Magnesium complex. The 3-in-1 blend of Glycinate, Citrate, and Malate seemed like a brilliant idea, combining the best of all worlds for relaxation, regularity, and energy. At first, the effects were noticeable. The Glycinate seemed to help with sleep, and the Citrate gave a gentle nudge to my digestive system without the usual urgency of other brands. The Malate component felt like it was contributing to a slight increase in my afternoon focus. However, my enthusiasm waned when I took a closer look at the label. The "1800mg" in the product title is a clever, but ultimately misleading, headline. A quick calculation reveals that the actual elemental magnesium is only 384mg per serving. While 384mg is a solid dose and within the recommended daily intake for most people, it's not the massive 1800mg the title suggests. The 1800mg figure refers to the total weight of the three magnesium compounds before the magnesium is separated from its bonded molecule (glycine, citric acid, malic acid). This kind of marketing is common in the supplement world, but it feels particularly deceptive here. Furthermore, the capsules themselves are quite large. For someone who has trouble swallowing pills, this could be a major drawback. I also noticed that the blend, while well-intentioned, didn't seem to deliver the full punch of a pure Magnesium Glycinate supplement when it came to deep relaxation. It felt more like a jack-of-all-trades, master-of-none situation. In conclusion, this is not a bad product. The quality seems good, and the combination of forms is a unique selling point. However, the misleading marketing and the slightly muted effects for specific goals (like deep sleep) prevent me from giving it a higher score. If you're looking for a general magnesium supplement and are aware of the actual elemental dosage, this could be a decent option. But if you're seeking a specific benefit and are sensitive to marketing claims, you might want to look elsewhere. Read more Read less 1,617 people found this helpful Helpful Sending feedback...
